quizName: DMV Practice Test #12 30 Questions • Passing Score 24

questions.question: Which color will make you harder to see?
questions.explanation: Wear bright colors like orange, red, yellow, or green to stay visible. Avoid dark or dull colors while riding.

questions.question: When should you increase your following distance?
questions.explanation: Increase your following distance when it takes longer to stop, when you cannot see ahead clearly, or when traffic is heavy.

questions.question: What material should riding gloves be made of?
questions.explanation: Riding gloves should be made of leather or similar durable material for grip and protection.

questions.question: What should you know about taking over-the-counter medication before riding?

options.text: It is usually safe because over-the-counter medications are weak.
It may affect your riding and should be done carefully.

questions.correctAnswerText: It may affect your riding and should be done carefully.
questions.explanation: Many medications, both prescription and over-the-counter, can affect your ability to ride safely. Talk to your doctor about how any new medication may affect your riding.

questions.question: Where are you most likely to have a conflict with other vehicles?
questions.explanation: Intersections are where most conflicts happen between motorcycles and other vehicles.

questions.question: When it starts to rain, where should you ride?

options.text: On the right side of the lane.
On the edge of the road.
In the tire tracks left by cars.

questions.correctAnswerText: In the tire tracks left by cars.
questions.explanation: When rain starts, the road becomes slippery from rain mixing with oil left by cars. Ride in the tire tracks of cars ahead of you for better grip.

questions.question: Which is NOT a way to control your motorcycle in a turn?
questions.explanation: To turn safely, slow down before the turn, look where you want to go, lean into the turn, and gently accelerate through it.

questions.question: What is true about reflective, brightly-colored helmets and clothing?

options.text: You should only wear them at night.
They help other drivers see you.

questions.correctAnswerText: They help other drivers see you.
questions.explanation: Bright or reflective clothing increases your visibility to other drivers.

questions.question: What gear should your motorcycle be in when starting the engine?
questions.explanation: Always start your motorcycle with the transmission in neutral. Your speedometer will show a neutral indicator light when this is set correctly.

questions.question: How should you handle someone tailgating you?

options.text: Slow down or change lanes to let them pass.
Speed up to increase distance between you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down or change lanes to let them pass.
questions.explanation: If safe, change lanes and let the tailgater pass. Speeding up makes the danger worse.

questions.question: A person is considered intoxicated at a blood alcohol content (BAC) of ____ or higher.
questions.explanation: In Virginia, a BAC of 0.08 percent or higher means a person is intoxicated. An intoxicated person cannot legally operate a motor vehicle.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: Regulatory signs are white with red and black markings. They tell drivers about traffic laws in that area. This sign means U-turns are not allowed.

questions.question: When riding, you should wear:
questions.explanation: Wear bright colors to make yourself visible to other drivers, even during the day. Clothes with reflective materials are also helpful.

questions.question: When passing parked vehicles on your right with no oncoming traffic, you should ride:

options.text: In the left portion of your lane.
In the right portion of your lane.
In the center of your lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: In the left portion of your lane.
questions.explanation: Ride in the left portion of your lane when passing parked cars on your right and there is no oncoming traffic. This helps you avoid opened car doors and people stepping out between vehicles. If there is oncoming traffic, stay in the center of your lane for more space around you.

questions.question: A solid white line on the side of the road indicates:

options.text: The right edge of a traffic lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: The right edge of a traffic lane.
questions.explanation: A solid white line on the side of the road marks the right edge of a traffic lane.

questions.question: To shift to a higher gear, you must:

options.text: Place your foot under the shift lever and lift.
Place your foot over the shift lever and push.
Use your thumb to move the lever.

questions.correctAnswerText: Place your foot under the shift lever and lift.
questions.explanation: To shift up to a higher gear, place your foot under the shift lever and lift it.

questions.question: When riding a motorcycle:

options.text: The mirrors provide a perfect view.
The mirrors do not show your blind spots.
The mirrors should not be used, except when parking.

questions.correctAnswerText: The mirrors do not show your blind spots.
questions.explanation: Motorcycle mirrors have blind spots, just like any vehicle. Always turn your head to check for traffic in your blind spot before changing lanes.

questions.question: A protective jacket should:

options.text: Be loose-fitting and flap in the wind while riding.

questions.explanation: Riding clothes should protect you and keep you comfortable. Jackets and pants should fit snug enough so they do not flap in the wind, but loose enough to let you move freely.

questions.question: __________ can cause motorcycle collisions.
questions.explanation: Following too closely (tailgating) is a major cause of motorcycle collisions. Always keep a safe distance from the vehicle in front of you.

questions.question: Service signs are:
questions.explanation: Blue signs with white letters show where services are located. Services include rest areas, gas stations, food, and hospitals.

questions.question: When choosing a helmet, make sure it:
questions.explanation: Choose a helmet that meets U.S. Department of Transportation (DOT) and state standards. It should fit snugly and have no cracks, loose padding, or frayed straps.

questions.question: Which is NOT a benefit of keeping space between your motorcycle and other vehicles?

options.text: You will have time to react to hazards.
You will have space to maneuver.
You will have more time to accelerate when entering a curve.

questions.correctAnswerText: You will have more time to accelerate when entering a curve.
questions.explanation: Keeping space around your motorcycle helps you react to mistakes by others and gives you room to maneuver.

questions.question: A motorcycle passenger should:

options.text: Put their feet on the ground when the motorcycle is stopped.
Not ride without a back rest.
Sit as far forward as possible without crowding the operator.

questions.correctAnswerText: Sit as far forward as possible without crowding the operator.
questions.explanation: A passenger should sit as far forward as possible without crowding the operator. The passenger should keep both feet on the footrests at all times, even when stopped.

questions.question: Reflective clothing should be worn:
questions.explanation: Most motorcycle crashes happen during daylight. Wear brightly-colored, reflective clothing anytime you ride.

questions.question: Locking your brakes can:
questions.explanation: Locked brakes can cause control problems. If your front brake locks, release it and re-apply it. If your rear brake locks on a surface with good grip, keep it locked until you stop.

questions.question: To reduce the chance of a crash, you should:
questions.explanation: To reduce crashes, be visible, signal your intentions, keep space around you, look ahead at least 12 seconds, identify hazards, and be ready to react to changes.

questions.question: When a rider wears a helmet during a crash, they are:

options.text: Less likely to survive than someone without a helmet.
Just as likely to survive as someone without a helmet.
More likely to survive than someone without a helmet.

questions.correctAnswerText: More likely to survive than someone without a helmet.
questions.explanation: Riders without helmets are three times more likely to die from head injuries than riders with helmets, regardless of speed.

questions.question: If your rear wheel locks while stopping on a surface with good traction, you should:

options.text: Keep the wheel locked until you have stopped completely.
Release the rear brake and only use the front brake.
Release the rear brake and then quickly re-apply the brake.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep the wheel locked until you have stopped completely.
questions.explanation: If your rear wheel locks on a surface with good traction, you can keep it locked until you stop. You can still control your motorcycle if it is upright and going straight.

questions.question: To turn safely on a motorcycle, you should always:

options.text: Lean in the direction of the curve.
Turn by using only the handle bars.

questions.correctAnswerText: Lean in the direction of the curve.
questions.explanation: When turning, lean in the direction of the turn. Slow down before entering the turn.

questions.question: Blind spots on motorcycles:

options.text: Should be checked regularly by riders.
Don't exist if the motorcycle has a rearview mirror.

questions.correctAnswerText: Should be checked regularly by riders.
questions.explanation: Motorcycles have blind spots like any vehicle. Always turn your head to check for traffic in your blind spot before changing lanes. Make head checks part of your normal riding routine.
